assigned_texts.author: Manuel Academy
assigned_texts.source: Authored for Manuel Academy High School ELA; Academy-held rights.

assigned_texts.source: U.S. National Archives (federal government work, public domain)

essential_question: How does close, evidence-governed attention to strong and thorough textual evidence change what a reader or writer is entitled to claim?
learning_objectives: Explain what strong and thorough textual evidence means and name the textual signal that tells you it is in play.
Apply strong and thorough textual evidence to an assigned text using the stated criteria, working in the grades 9-10 text complexity band, with scaffolding available at the high end of the range.
Check the work against the criteria checklist and name one revision it calls for.
success_criteria: The response uses the criteria checklist and meets each item on it.
Every claim is tied to a specific, quoted or located piece of text.
The learner names one revision the checklist calls for and makes it.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
the unit's assigned texts, in an accessible reading representation
citation reference or style manual appropriate to the course

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a short retrieval prompt on strong and thorough textual evidence. Ask the learner to predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.
Ask the learner to attempt strong and thorough textual evidence cold, before any instruction. Record what they already do well. Nothing here is scored, and errors here are data, not failure.
Name what the diagnostic revealed in neutral, non-character language. State the unit question and what will count as evidence by the end of it.

Walk the unit's destination: Build an evidence-and-inference casebook on an unfamiliar text and defend two contested readings in seminar.. The learner writes down what they think will be hardest about it and why. The tutor may question this prediction but may not write it.
The learner records one specific thing about strong and thorough textual evidence they intend to be able to do by the end of the unit.

student_activity: Attempt strong and thorough textual evidence without instruction, then record a personal goal for the unit.
formative_check: Name one thing about strong and thorough textual evidence you can already do and one you cannot do yet.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid readings when the evidence supports them. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for strong and thorough textual evidence, re-teach it on a short passage, then retry one fresh item. Do not write the learner's response.
Ask the learner to explain why the move for strong and thorough textual evidence works on this text before continuing. Accept explanation in any modality.
Name specifically what the reasoning got right about strong and thorough textual evidence, offer one varied case, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Describe the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a correct case, and schedule a short later review of strong and thorough textual evidence.
Decline to supply the assessed response. Offer a question, a criterion, or a counterexample instead, and record that guided support was given.
Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate independent application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one of them on a text the learner has not seen before.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate independent application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one of them on a text the learner has not seen before.
extension: Apply the move to an unfamiliar passage of comparable complexity with the checklist available.
student_authorship: The learner writes every assessed response. The tutor may explain, question, critique, or suggest a revision direction.
The tutor must not draft, rewrite, or supply sentences for an assessed response, and must not complete a graded task on the learner's behalf.
Tutor assistance is logged as guided evidence; unaided work is logged as independent evidence. Mastery requires independent evidence.
Fixed-form assessment items keep their answer key adult-only; the key is never surfaced in a learner-facing surface.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and make the success criteria visible in text.
Allow typed, handwritten, dictated, or recorded-to-text responses; the response mode is not the standard.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, transcripts, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Provide an accessible reading representation (digital reflowable text, enlarged print, or audio) for every assigned text.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about writing and reading difficulty.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Offer an alternate text or private response when content is personally sensitive.
Do not require autobiographical disclosure; fictionalized or analytical alternatives are always acceptable.
Presentation may be delivered privately to the facilitator; no public or recorded performance is ever required.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, annotated passage, recorded reading, or short clip supporting strong and thorough textual evidence.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable text, alt text, or a transcript. No media is required to meet the standard.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw drafts, raw private reflections, recordings, or diagnosis language.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one real-world instance of strong and thorough textual evidence in something they already read. No purchase, account creation, or private disclosure is required.
performance_task_link: Build an evidence-and-inference casebook on an unfamiliar text and defend two contested readings in seminar.

essential_question: How does close, evidence-governed attention to valid reasoning versus sufficient evidence change what a reader or writer is entitled to claim?
learning_objectives: Explain what valid reasoning versus sufficient evidence means and name the textual signal that tells you it is in play.

Apply valid reasoning versus sufficient evidence to an assigned text using the stated criteria, working in the grades 9-10 text complexity band, with scaffolding available at the high end of the range.
Check the work against the criteria checklist and name one revision it calls for.
success_criteria: The response uses the criteria checklist and meets each item on it.
Every claim is tied to a specific, quoted or located piece of text.
The learner names one revision the checklist calls for and makes it.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
the unit's assigned texts, in an accessible reading representation
citation reference or style manual appropriate to the course

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a short retrieval prompt on valid reasoning versus sufficient evidence. Ask the learner to predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.
Name the move, show a worked example on a short passage, and make the success criteria explicit before practice begins. Keep the explanation centered on valid reasoning versus sufficient evidence.

Work two supported examples together. After each step ask, "What in the text licenses that move?" Fade prompts on the second example. The object of practice is valid reasoning versus sufficient evidence.

The learner completes a new application with the criteria checklist still available, recording the result and the reasoning that produced it. The learner writes this response; the tutor may question or critique but may not draft it.
In one concise response, state the most important claim about valid reasoning versus sufficient evidence and one check that would expose a weak or unsupported reading.

student_activity: The learner completes a new application with the criteria checklist still available, recording the result and the reasoning that produced it. Focus: valid reasoning versus sufficient evidence.
formative_check: State the most important claim about valid reasoning versus sufficient evidence and identify one check that would expose a weak or unsupported reading.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid readings when the evidence supports them. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for valid reasoning versus sufficient evidence, re-teach it on a short passage, then retry one fresh item. Do not write the learner's response.
Ask the learner to explain why the move for valid reasoning versus sufficient evidence works on this text before continuing. Accept explanation in any modality.
Name specifically what the reasoning got right about valid reasoning versus sufficient evidence, offer one varied case, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Describe the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a correct case, and schedule a short later review of valid reasoning versus sufficient evidence.
Decline to supply the assessed response. Offer a question, a criterion, or a counterexample instead, and record that guided support was given.
Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate independent application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one of them on a text the learner has not seen before.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate independent application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one of them on a text the learner has not seen before.
extension: Apply the move to an unfamiliar passage of comparable complexity with the checklist available.
student_authorship: The learner writes every assessed response. The tutor may explain, question, critique, or suggest a revision direction.
The tutor must not draft, rewrite, or supply sentences for an assessed response, and must not complete a graded task on the learner's behalf.
Tutor assistance is logged as guided evidence; unaided work is logged as independent evidence. Mastery requires independent evidence.
Fixed-form assessment items keep their answer key adult-only; the key is never surfaced in a learner-facing surface.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and make the success criteria visible in text.
Allow typed, handwritten, dictated, or recorded-to-text responses; the response mode is not the standard.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, transcripts, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Provide an accessible reading representation (digital reflowable text, enlarged print, or audio) for every assigned text.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about writing and reading difficulty.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.

essential_question: How does close, evidence-governed attention to strategic and accessible digital media change what a reader or writer is entitled to claim?
learning_objectives: Explain what strategic and accessible digital media means and name the textual signal that tells you it is in play.
Apply strategic and accessible digital media to an assigned text using the stated criteria, working in the grades 9-10 text complexity band, with scaffolding available at the high end of the range.
Check the work against the criteria checklist and name one revision it calls for.
success_criteria: The response uses the criteria checklist and meets each item on it.
Every claim is tied to a specific, quoted or located piece of text.
The learner names one revision the checklist calls for and makes it.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
the unit's assigned texts, in an accessible reading representation
citation reference or style manual appropriate to the course

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: One last revision of the unit's product against the success criteria, focused on what is most significant for the audience.

Publish or present the work. This may be delivered publicly, privately to the facilitator, in writing, orally, or in another accessible format. No public or recorded performance is ever required, and media carries captions, transcripts, and alt text.
Place the piece beside earlier work and identify, with evidence, what changed about the learner's handling of strategic and accessible digital media and the unit's other topics.
Name what from this unit the next unit will assume you can already do.
File the piece with its target, evidence type, and revision history. Raw drafts and private reflections stay out of the guardian-visible record.

student_activity: Publish or present the unit's work in a chosen format, then evidence the growth it shows.
formative_check: Point to one concrete difference between this piece and your earlier work, and name what caused it.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid readings when the evidence supports them. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for strategic and accessible digital media, re-teach it on a short passage, then retry one fresh item. Do not write the learner's response.
Ask the learner to explain why the move for strategic and accessible digital media works on this text before continuing. Accept explanation in any modality.
Name specifically what the reasoning got right about strategic and accessible digital media, offer one varied case, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Describe the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a correct case, and schedule a short later review of strategic and accessible digital media.
Decline to supply the assessed response. Offer a question, a criterion, or a counterexample instead, and record that guided support was given.
Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate independent application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one of them on a text the learner has not seen before.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate independent application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one of them on a text the learner has not seen before.
extension: Apply the move to an unfamiliar passage of comparable complexity with the checklist available.
student_authorship: The learner writes every assessed response. The tutor may explain, question, critique, or suggest a revision direction.
The tutor must not draft, rewrite, or supply sentences for an assessed response, and must not complete a graded task on the learner's behalf.
Tutor assistance is logged as guided evidence; unaided work is logged as independent evidence. Mastery requires independent evidence.
Fixed-form assessment items keep their answer key adult-only; the key is never surfaced in a learner-facing surface.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and make the success criteria visible in text.
Allow typed, handwritten, dictated, or recorded-to-text responses; the response mode is not the standard.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, transcripts, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Provide an accessible reading representation (digital reflowable text, enlarged print, or audio) for every assigned text.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about writing and reading difficulty.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Offer an alternate text or private response when content is personally sensitive.
Do not require autobiographical disclosure; fictionalized or analytical alternatives are always acceptable.
Presentation may be delivered privately to the facilitator; no public or recorded performance is ever required.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, annotated passage, recorded reading, or short clip supporting strategic and accessible digital media.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable text, alt text, or a transcript. No media is required to meet the standard.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw drafts, raw private reflections, recordings, or diagnosis language.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one real-world instance of strategic and accessible digital media in something they already read. No purchase, account creation, or private disclosure is required.
performance_task_link: Publish a curated portfolio and formally defend one piece against questions about its evidence, revision history, and source use.
